title: MedConstBench: Benchmarking How Constitutions Steer LLMs in Medical Ethics
abstract: arXiv:2610.36513v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: As large language models advance rapidly, they are increasingly used to answer medical questions, and many such models are now deployed locally. Once a model is deployed, its behavior is governed mainly by the ethical policy written into its constitution. However, most existing work focuses on factual correctness rather than the trade-off between competing ethical values. Even benchmarks that do evaluate ethics treat it as a fixed property of the model rather than as a variable, so how a constitution reshapes medical-ethics behavior remains largely unexplored. We introduce MedConstBench, a medical-ethics benchmark that treats the deployment constitution as a controlled variable, is organized around Beauchamp's four principles, and is scored by human-calibrated multi-model peer review. translated_title: MedConstBench：衡量“宪法”如何引导大语言模型医疗伦理行为的基准测试
translated_abstract: 随着大语言模型的快速发展，它们被越来越多地用于回答医学问题，且许多此类模型如今已在本地部署。模型一旦部署，其行为主要由写入其“宪法”中的伦理政策所决定。然而，现有研究大多关注事实正确性，而非相互冲突的伦理价值之间的权衡。即使是那些确实评估伦理的基准测试，也将伦理视为模型的固定属性而非变量，因此“宪法”如何重塑医疗伦理行为在很大程度上仍未被探索。我们提出 MedConstBench，一个将部署宪法作为受控变量的医疗伦理基准测试，它围绕比彻姆的四大伦理原则组织，并通过人工校准的多模型同行评审进行评分。该基准包含我们自主构建的临床困境数据集 MedDilemma，并支持对“宪法”如何引导大语言模型进行系统性分析。对十个开源（模型）的评估……
tldr: 该论文提出 MedConstBench，首个将部署“宪法”作为受控变量、围绕比彻姆四大伦理原则构建、并通过人工校准的多模型同行评审评分的医疗伦理基准，实现了对宪法如何引导大语言模型医疗伦理行为的系统分析。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces MedConstBench, the first medical-ethics benchmark that treats the deployment constitution as a controlled variable, is organized around Beauchamp's four principles, and is scored by human-calibrated multi-model peer review, enabling systematic analysis of how constitutions steer LLMs' medical-ethics behavior.
